title: Find and Replace Pattern
summary: Given a list of strings and a pattern, return a list of words that match the pattern through a one-to-one letter mapping.
statement: Given a list of strings and a pattern, return a list of words that match the pattern through a one-to-one letter mapping. You may return the matching words in any order. A word matches the pattern if there exists a bijection such that replacing every letter in the pattern with its corresponding letter in the bijection results in the word.
constraints: A word matches when a bijection replaces pattern letters to form it.
Return all matching words in any order.
hints: Bijective renaming preserves the sequence of first-occurrence IDs.
Canonicalize both word and pattern by assigning each new character its next ID.
Keep words whose canonical ID list equals the pattern’s list.
Equal canonical forms establish a one-to-one correspondence in both directions.
editorial: Equal canonical forms establish a one-to-one correspondence in both directions.

tests.explanation: Mee and aqq share the pattern of one letter followed by a repeated second letter.
